interpretation: Structural validity and traceability do not establish completeness or learner readiness. Higher-level sources, alternate paths, and other source outcomes are inspection signals, not automatic defects. Do not delete edges or split decks without evaluating their contracts.

exclusions.subject: mathematics
exclusions.rationale: Specialist derived geometry and categorical foundations are beyond the representative continuation; algebraic foundations remain in mathematics/commutative-algebra:module-and-local-methods,algebraic-varieties.

exclusions.subject: computer-science

exclusions.subject: physics

exclusions.subject: chemistry

outcomes.description: Infer temperature, distance and luminosity from calibrated spectra and photometry.
Infer orbital and galactic masses from kinematic observations with selection caveats.
Construct stellar hydrostatic and energy-balance models and interpret evolutionary tracks.

practice: Analyze a calibrated stellar catalog and spectra, reconstructing physical quantities and selection limitations.

includes: Driven two-level systems, lasers and coherence
Photon statistics and optical quantum measurements

outcomes.description: Calculate atomic transition structures and intensities using angular momentum and perturbations.
Analyze driven and dissipative quantum systems, coherent control and laser rate models.
Interpret photon-counting and coherence measurements with explicit detector and state models.

practice: Derive driven-state predictions and analyze supplied atomic spectra and photon-correlation data.

includes: Metropolis and kinetic Monte Carlo methods

outcomes.description: Implement Monte Carlo sampling for specified physical distributions and estimate correlated errors.
Implement particle dynamics and finite-difference field models with physical boundary conditions.
Test conservation, discretization convergence, finite-size effects and benchmark agreement.

practice: Implement a particle simulator, field solver and supplied-distribution sampler with independent validation tests.

includes: Magnetism, superconductivity and topological band examples

outcomes.description: Derive phonon and electronic band models and connect reciprocal-space structure to measurements.
Analyze magnetic, superconducting and elementary topological phases using explicit model Hamiltonians.
Calculate elementary transport and response functions and interpret experimental signatures.

practice: Derive band and collective-state models and compare predicted spectra, heat capacities and transport signatures.

includes: Viscous flow, diffusion and nondimensional scaling
Waves and linear stability in fluids

outcomes.description: Derive mass, momentum and energy balances using stress and constitutive relations.
Solve standard viscous-flow and transport problems and identify dimensionless regimes.
Analyze elementary fluid waves and linear instabilities under bounded assumptions.

practice: Derive laminar-flow and transport solutions and compare scaled laboratory or supplied flow measurements.

includes: Charge, electric field, voltage and current
Resistance, capacitance and DC circuit laws

outcomes.description: Solve DC resistor networks and calculate capacitor charge and stored energy.
Distinguish charge, field, potential and current using diagrams and energy accounting.

practice: Predict and measure safe low-voltage circuit behavior using schematics and meter readings.

outcomes.description: Transform electromagnetic tensors and derive covariant field and force relations.
Solve electromagnetic boundary problems with multipoles and Green-function methods.
Derive retarded fields and calculate standard radiation patterns and power.

practice: Derive boundary and radiation solutions and check gauge, energy and Lorentz consistency.

outcomes.description: Model polarization, magnetization and conduction under stated constitutive assumptions.
Use Maxwell equations to derive induction, wave propagation and energy conservation.
Calculate static fields and potentials using symmetry, integration and boundary conditions.

practice: Solve field-boundary problems using diagrams, integral laws and differential consistency checks.

outcomes.description: Design transistor and operational-amplifier circuits and derive filter transfer responses.
Measure gain, bandwidth and noise and validate an instrument against specifications.
Integrate sensors, converters and digital timing with explicit sampling and aliasing constraints.

practice: Build and characterize a safe sensor amplifier and acquisition chain using frequency-response and noise measurements.

includes: Optical and electrical signals; Fourier representation

outcomes.description: Design controlled measurements with calibration, repeatability and systematic-error budgets.
Estimate physical parameters and compare models using residuals and propagated uncertainty.
Acquire optical and electrical signals and interpret sampling and Fourier spectra with supplied tools.

practice: Measure an optical or electrical response, calibrate it and reconstruct parameters with an uncertainty budget.

includes: Einstein equations and standard spacetime solutions

outcomes.description: Derive homogeneous cosmological evolution and constrain parameters from distance and expansion data.
Formulate Einstein equations and analyze standard symmetric spacetime solutions.
Calculate geodesic, lensing and linear gravitational-wave observables.

practice: Calculate observables in standard metrics and compare cosmological distance models with supplied measurements.

outcomes.description: Choose and apply energy and momentum conservation to constrained interactions.
Formulate and solve Newtonian motion problems using vector force models.
Calculate rotational dynamics and orbital quantities for standard mass distributions.

practice: Derive and test motion predictions from force diagrams, integrals and conservation equations.

includes: Nuclear binding, shell and collective models

outcomes.description: Calculate decay chains, reaction energetics and elementary cross-section relations.
Compare binding, shell and collective models against nuclear properties.
Infer radiation energies and activities using detector response, efficiency and background models.

practice: Interpret archived radiation spectra and reaction data using calibrated response and uncertainty models.

includes: Standard Model fields, symmetries and interactions

outcomes.description: Reconstruct bounded collision observables and estimate signal yields with acceptance and background models.
Explain Standard Model representations, gauge interactions and symmetry breaking quantitatively.
Assess symmetry and precision tests using competing physical hypotheses and systematic uncertainties.

practice: Analyze a supplied collision dataset with taught event reconstruction, efficiency corrections and hypothesis comparisons.

includes: Motion, energy, heat and interactions conceptually

outcomes.description: Explain conservation, interactions and heat transfer in everyday systems.
Check dimensions and report repeated measurements with resolution and spread.
Construct motion graphs, force diagrams and idealized physical models.

practice: Measure motion and cooling; compare graphical predictions with repeated observations and instrument resolution.

outcomes.description: Analyze magnetohydrodynamic equilibria, waves and standard instabilities.
Infer plasma density and temperature using probe and emission models with validity checks.
Derive screening and elementary kinetic plasma behavior from distribution models.

practice: Derive dispersion relations and infer plasma parameters from supplied diagnostic measurements.

outcomes.description: Derive classical field equations and quantize scalar, spinor and gauge-field examples.
Construct perturbative amplitudes and evaluate standard tree and bounded one-loop examples.
Apply regularization and renormalization to simple theories and explain effective-theory limits.

practice: Derive amplitudes and renormalized observables for bounded field models with symmetry and dimensional checks.

includes: Hilbert notation, operators and Schrodinger dynamics

outcomes.description: Use angular-momentum algebra and spin to analyze central-potential states.
Apply perturbation, variational and semiclassical approximations with validity checks.
Solve standard Schrodinger problems and calculate operator probabilities and expectation values.

practice: Solve bound-state and tunneling problems and compare exact and approximate energy predictions.

includes: Photons, matter waves and discrete spectra

outcomes.description: Use photon and matter-wave relations to interpret spectra and interference evidence.
Distinguish amplitudes, probabilities, superposition and measurement using two-state examples.

practice: Compare classical and quantum predictions for supplied photoelectric, diffraction and two-state datasets.

outcomes.description: Calculate Lorentz transformations and interpret simultaneity and causal intervals geometrically.
Use four-momentum conservation to solve relativistic decay and collision problems.

practice: Solve observer-comparison and collision problems using spacetime diagrams and invariant quantities.

includes: Microcanonical, canonical and grand canonical ensembles

outcomes.description: Derive ensemble distributions and calculate partition functions and thermodynamic observables.
Analyze fluctuations, response and elementary phase-transition models using correlations.
Calculate ideal Bose and Fermi system properties and classical limits.

practice: Derive ensemble predictions and compare finite-system, continuum and thermodynamic limits.

includes: State variables and thermal equations of state
First and second laws; thermodynamic potentials

outcomes.description: Use entropy and thermodynamic potentials to assess equilibrium and irreversibility.
Analyze engine and refrigeration cycles and identify efficiency bounds.
Calculate work, heat and state changes for simple compressible systems.

practice: Reconcile energy and entropy budgets across reversible and irreversible cycles using state diagrams.

outcomes.description: Construct ray diagrams and calculate image positions, magnification and resolution limits.
Calculate interference and elementary aperture diffraction from superposed amplitudes.
Derive harmonic and sinusoidal wave solutions and calculate energy and phase relations.

practice: Predict and measure lens images and fringe patterns, comparing amplitude and intensity representations.
